deviations.taskId: Milestone 1, step 4 (internal/config specFormat YAML mode) + deliverable "lifecycle.yml/config.Default() seed the YAML format vocabulary"
deviations.specSection: specs/spec-format/spec.md — "YAML is the source of truth for the living spec and spec deltas" (the tool must operate in YAML mode); design D1/D4
deviations.planSaid: Update internal/config so config.Default() (and lifecycle.yml) seed the YAML format vocabulary and the tool operates in YAML mode. M1's inferred path-set (from its deliverables/steps) is internal/spec, internal/schema, internal/config, lifecycle.yml, and go.mod/go.sum. internal/scaffold is NOT named by any M1 deliverable or step, and the M1 validation contract runs tests only for ./internal/spec/... ./internal/schema/... ./internal/config/...
deviations.intendedChange: config.Default() now seeds SpecFormat.Grammar = config.GrammarYAML ("yaml") instead of the old OpenSpec markdown pin "1.5.0" (required by the M1 deliverable). This invalidates a coupled assertion in internal/scaffold/init_test.go (TestRunInit_FreshRepoWritesEverything, ~line 114) which asserts the seeded config's Grammar == "1.5.0". The needed fix is a one-line update of that expectation to config.GrammarYAML. internal/scaffold is outside M1's path-set, so I am NOT making that edit; I am logging it and halting on it for approval.
deviations.reason: The change to config.Default() is an explicit, required M1 deliverable, but the only file that must change to keep `go test ./internal/scaffold/...` green is outside M1's inferred path-set. Per working rules 3 and 5, an out-of-path edit is a logged deviation, never a silent decision.
deviations.blastRadius: One assertion line in one test file (internal/scaffold/init_test.go); no production code. internal/scaffold's runtime behavior is unchanged — RunInit already relays whatever config.Default() seeds; only the test's hard-coded expected grammar string is stale. M1's own declared validation criteria (CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./... ; go test ./internal/spec/... ./internal/schema/... ./internal/config/...) are unaffected and pass.
